rust.fuzzing_or_property_tests: manual property-style test (monotonic invariant), with no external dependency; real fuzzing would require proptest or cargo-fuzz (external crates)
rust.file_locking: standard library, portable (cfg(unix) used in the spike for simplicity, but std::fs::File::lock exists cross-platform since Rust 1.89)
rust.subprocess_cancellation_approach: manual poll with try_wait() + kill() + wait(); never blocks reading stdout on the timeout path, which naturally avoids the orphan holding the pipe open
rust.notable_finding: no post-hoc fix was needed; the initial implementation was correct on the first attempt

go.fuzzing_or_property_tests: real native fuzzing (go test -fuzz), with no external dependency; 384496 executions in 10s (~38000/s), 0 failures
go.file_locking: syscall.Flock, POSIX-only (macOS/Linux); would require a separate implementation (LockFileEx) for Windows
go.subprocess_cancellation_approach: real finding: the idiomatic form (exec.CommandContext + cmd.Output()) does NOT cancel in time because of the orphaned-grandchild problem (sleep, a child of bash, keeps the stdout pipe open after only the direct process is killed). Fixed by using Setpgid + kill(-pid) on the whole process group.
go.notable_finding: it required a fix: the first implementation (idiomatic, with cmd.Output()) took 5016ms to cancel a 500ms timeout; the version fixed with process groups does meet the deadline

comparison_summary.mcp_latency: comparable, both in single-digit or low double-digit milliseconds
comparison_summary.cancellation_correctness: Rust correct on the first attempt; Go required a fix after a real finding of a known idiomatic footgun in the standard library
comparison_summary.fuzzing_ergonomics: Go: native in the standard library. Rust: would require an external dependency (proptest/cargo-fuzz), not tested in this spike to keep dependency parity
